name: Adams Air Force Base
description: Runways and hangars the Enclave claimed as a staging ground; the old jets never left.

name: Arefu
description: Shacks straddle a cracked overpass, ropes and ladders doing the work of streets.

name: Big Town
description: Sandbagged and full of kids who fled Little Lamplight and never looked back.

name: Bunker Hill
description: Traders crowd under a pre-war obelisk, caravans at the gate and prices at the throat.

name: Cambridge
description: Broken laboratories and a police station holding the line on the square.

name: Canterbury Commons
description: Two costumed idiots once warred over these rooftops; the town still talks about it.

name: Concord
description: A ruined town square of sandbags and raider camps, its museum the only thing standing proud.

name: County Crossing
description: A tanning rack, a water pump, and a shack or two on the road east of the city.

name: Covenant
description: Whitewashed walls and a lot of questions before anyone opens the gate.

name: Diamond City
description: A ballpark turned city, the great green wall glowing over a market that never stops haggling.

name: Filly
description: Hardscrabble hamlet north of the city, trading salvage for anything it cannot grow.

name: Galaxy News Radio
description: A radio tower and a DJ's booth, broadcasting the old songs and the day's bad news.

name: Goodneighbor
description: Neon lights, misfits, and chems, ruled by a mayor with a knife and a grudge.

name: Graygarden
description: Mr. Handys tend neat rows atop an overpass, forever short one supervisor.

name: Hollywood
description: Ruined marquees and studios still sell illusions to anyone with caps.

name: Jamaica Plain
description: A suburb swallowed by the city's sprawl, its buried treasure vault sealed since before the war.

name: Jefferson Memorial
description: A marble memorial to a dead president, its rotunda now a water purifier and a battleground.

name: Lexington
description: A factory town gone quiet, its streets a shooting gallery and its plant still running on ghosts.

name: Little Lamplight
description: Children hold a cave warren and banish anyone at sixteen; the gate is rocks and nerve.

name: Megaton
description: A scrap town ringed around an unexploded bomb, its church and its curse in equal measure.

name: National Archives
description: Vaults and file rooms guard a declaration worth more than most armies.

name: Novac
description: A motel strip under a fiberglass dinosaur, the best sniper perch for a hundred miles.

name: Nuka-World
description: A ruined amusement park of Nuka-Cola rides and raider gangs dividing the wreckage.

name: Oberland Station
description: Tin roofs and a hand pump by the tracks, close enough to hear the city breathe.

name: Paradise Falls
description: A mall turned slaver camp, collar in one hand and a smile that does not reach the eyes.

name: Primm
description: Casinos and a roller coaster off the highway, still pointing at a sky it cannot reach.

name: Quincy
description: A walled settlement that fell to gunners, its barricades facing the wrong way now.

name: Raven Rock
description: Steel doors and quieter rooms: the mountain bunker where the Enclave runs its command.

name: Republic of Dave
description: One man's backyard kingdom, complete with elections, a flag, and nobody else's vote.

name: Rivet City
description: An aircraft carrier wedged in the river mud, its flight deck a market and its hull a wall.

name: Sanctuary Hills
description: A pre-war cul-de-sac of tidy homes gone feral, the kind of quiet that listens back.

name: Shady Sands
description: Farm village that grew into the NCR's heart, still dusty and still certain of itself.

name: Somerville Place
description: A small farmstead south of the city, corn in the yard and a wall built one board at a time.

name: Tenpenny Tower
description: A luxury tower behind a private army, its penthouse views paid for by someone below.

name: The Boneyard
description: The skeletal sprawl of old Los Angeles, picked clean and still worth the trip.

name: The Citadel
description: The Pentagon's shell, rebuilt into the Brotherhood's fortress, armor on the ramparts and no welcome.

name: The Institute
description: A shadowy research body beneath the Commonwealth, doing its work and denying yours.

name: The Nucleus
description: A Children of Atom stronghold inside a beached submarine, glowing and unbothered.

name: The Slog
description: Ghouls work a tarberry farm in an old swimming pool, the one crop that asks nothing.

name: Vault 32
description: An experiment sealed behind a Vault-Tec door, its corridors quiet and its records wrong.

name: Vault 33
description: A Vault-Tec community that kept its decency and its door, right up until it could not.

name: Vault 101
description: A sealed Vault-Tec door, three generations deep, run like a school with a gun rack.

name: Vault 111
description: Cryopods and ice sleep under this hillside door, where the world ended twice and one woke.

name: Appalachia
description: Green hills and deep mines, where the Scorched walked and the Responders did not come back.

name: Big MT
description: A pre-war research crater of mad science, its labs gone quiet and its machines opinionated.

name: Far Harbor
description: Fog soaks an island off the Maine coast, its harbors hiding more than fish.

name: Fort Hagen
description: Old parade grounds, now a sniper's nest, the fort's orders still tacked to the wall.

name: Mass Pike Tunnel
description: A flooded highway tunnel under the Mass Pike, a shortcut that costs anyone who takes it.

name: Museum of Freedom
description: A colonial museum holding a suit of power armor and the Minutemen's last stand.

name: Point Lookout
description: A tidal marsh of boardwalks and inbred camps, the fog thick enough to swallow a lantern.

name: Poseidon Energy
description: A pre-war Poseidon Energy station, turbines dead and the grid still humming somewhere below.

name: Red Rocket
description: A Red Rocket stop on the roadside, its rocket sign still standing, its pumps long dry.

name: Starlight Drive-In
description: A cracked drive-in with a dead screen and a lot of open ground nobody guards well.

name: Vault-Tec HQ
description: Vault-Tec's regional offices, the paperwork gone quiet and the safes still full of promises.

name: the Capital Wasteland
description: The cratered bones of Washington, where the Metro maps matter more than the streets.

name: the Commonwealth
description: Boston's ruins and its outskirts, torn between the Institute and everyone it haunts.

name: the Divide
description: A storm-cut canyon of collapsed highways and buried silos, marked by old missiles.

name: the Glowing Sea
description: A crater of mashed suburbs and constant rads, where the sky itself looks wrong.

name: the Mojave desert
description: Scrub, sand, and broken highway, split between the NCR, the Legion, and Mr. House.

name: Zion Canyon
description: Red cliffs and green riverbottom, kept by the tribes and the Burned Man who guards it.

name: the Pitt
description: A smoking steel city of slag and slaves, churning out the one thing the wasteland still buys.

name: Nuka-Cola Plant
description: The Nuka-Cola bottling plant, its lines stopped and its syrup still rationed like gold.

name: Vault 274
description: Unexplored vault signal — raiding available in a future update.

name: Vault 077
description: Unexplored vault signal — raiding available in a future update.

name: Vault 871
description: Unexplored vault signal — raiding available in a future update.

name: Vault 242
description: Unexplored vault signal — raiding available in a future update.

name: Vault 521
description: Unexplored vault signal — raiding available in a future update.

name: Red Rocket - Springvale
description: The Red Rocket guarding Springvale's road, picked over and still good for a breather.

name: Red Rocket - Cambridge
description: A Red Rocket at the Cambridge edge, close enough to the city to be watched.

name: Super Duper Mart
description: Shelves stripped bare at the Super Duper Mart, the stockroom the only mystery left.

name: Super Duper Mart - Quincy
description: A second Super Duper Mart near Quincy, shelves bare but the back rooms never quite cleared.

name: The Quiet Zone
description: A chain of rusted fences around an abandoned industrial complex. Scavengers insist the air bends after radstorms and that shiny things appear where nobody left them. Engineers insist the scavengers drink too much.

name: Boston
description: The old colonial capital, a labyrinth of alleys where every block knows your business.

name: Boston Airport
description: Grounded runways the Brotherhood turned into a fortress of scrap plating and vertibirds.

name: Enclave Facility
description: A hidden Enclave installation, its laboratories sealed and its experiments left running.

name: Flagstaff
description: Caesar's seat of power, a city that answers to the Legion and little else.

name: Goodsprings
description: A one-saloon town at the edge of the Mojave, where the water is clean and the welcome is thin.

name: Hoover Dam
description: The Hoover Dam still turns the Colorado into power, still fought over by everyone downstream.

name: Jacobstown
description: Super mutants and nightkin keep a mountain retreat orderly, watched by a sheriff with a long memory.

name: Las Vegas
description: Neon still burns on the Strip, fenced off from the tribes that would tear it down.

name: Los Angeles
description: The old city sprawls for miles, its freeways a canyon system for anyone who can map it.

name: Mojave Outpost
description: Two statues and a chain-link gate: the NCR's line between the Mojave and the long road west.

name: Mount Charleston
description: Pines cover this mountain above the desert, cold enough to keep the worst of it at bay.

name: Railroad HQ
description: Under an old church, a hidden bolt-hole where the Railroad moves its people and its plans.

name: Vault 76
description: A Vault-Tec door that opened on Reclamation Day and never closed again.

name: Griffith Observatory
description: A white-domed observatory above the ruins, its telescope still pointed at a sky that answers nothing.
